claims.text: As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type thin films or nanoribbons have substantial substrate-induced interfacial strain.
Substrate-induced interfacial strain leads to prevalent magnetic-domain pinning in these nanoscale alloys.
Substrate-induced interfacial strain broadens the magnetostructural transition.
Strain-associated domain pinning and transition broadening increase hysteresis.
Strain-associated domain pinning and transition broadening suppress the low-field magnetocaloric response.
Controlled thermal annealing will partially relieve interfacial strain.
Partial strain relief will reduce magnetic-domain pinning.
Partial strain relief and reduced domain pinning will sharpen the magnetostructural transition.
Annealed samples will have lower hysteresis than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealed samples will have an enhanced low-field magnetocaloric response relative to the as-deposited baseline.
Thermal boundary resistance limits the maximum magnetic-cooling cycle frequency.
The predicted annealing improvements will be most notable at low cycling frequencies because heat-transfer limitations are less dominant there.
The predicted effects apply only at low applied fields and cycle frequencies below the heat-transfer limit imposed by thermal boundary resistance.
The relative contributions of thermal boundary resistance and magnetic-domain pinning have not been quantitatively decoupled.
